Hey Bryan — great talking earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call: 

- Use case: customer support summarization + reranking for priority routing.
- Main constraints: p95 latency target around 450ms, end-to-end throughput target ~120 TPS during peak, and strict PII handling (VPC desirable).

Recommended next steps:
1) Shared benchmark pack (attached) + Redwood-verified model profiles so you can see real latency percentiles and token throughput.
2) We recommend starting evaluation with two model variants: Llama-2-Chat-13B-q8_0 (best quality/throughput balance) and redwood-3b-qlora (low-cost, lower-latency option).
3) We'll run a short evaluation using your prompt set (please see attached acme_prompt_set_v1.txt) and a 1k-sample subset — we can run this in our sandbox within 48h.

Attachments: redwood_model_profiles_20260315.pdf, acme_prompt_set_v1.txt
Links: Console benchmark (https://console.redwood.ai/benchmarks/ACME-12345)

Notes on metrics we share: Redwood-verified profiles show p50/p95/p99 latency for token generation (server-side inference only) and estimated end-to-end TPS under our recommended batching and KV-cache settings. They also show results on standard sequence lengths (avg 128 tokens) and a high-memory scenario (avg 512).

Proposed meeting: 30-min sync after the eval run to review tradeoffs and next steps. Is Wed or Thu next week better for you?

— Alex

Thanks Bryan — answered inline below and included a few concrete numbers from our Redwood-verified profiles.

- p95/p99 latency at ~120 TPS (server-side token generation only, measured on a T4-equivalent pool with Redwood batching):
  * Llama-2-Chat-13B-q8_0: p50=60ms, p95=420ms, p99=780ms (avg token len 128, batching policy: dynamic batch up to 16)
  * redwood-3b-qlora: p50=28ms, p95=190ms, p99=360ms (same batching policy)

- Throughput: with our continuous batching & KV cache enabled we observed steady-state token throughput equivalent to ~130 TPS for the 13B q8_0 and ~230 TPS for the 3B qlora profile (this factors in typical user think-time gaps).

- Quality regression (quantized 13B vs fp16 baseline): on our eval suites we typically see a small degradation on fine-grained classification (~1.5-3% absolute drop on intent accuracy) and negligible change on summarization ROUGE for the prompt styles you shared. We surface regression alerts tied to your labeled validation set if you provide one.

I've uploaded the Redwood-verified performance profiles (redwood_model_profiles_20260315.pdf) and a starter benchmark CSV (acme_benchmark_results.csv) to the shared Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c

Next steps from our side:
- We'll run the 1k-sample eval using your prompt set (acme_prompt_set_v1.txt) and attach the raw outputs + token-level timing per sample.
- Jordan will coordinate the eval run and share the Doc link with results.

If the numbers above look reasonable, we'll schedule the run for Tuesday (48h).

— Alex

Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
